title: structured output: add regex/CFG constrained-decoding backends and tokenizer edgecase fixes
author: Priya Natarajan
description: Motivation: stabilize and standardize constrained decoding for structured outputs (CFG and regex constraints) by introducing pluggable decoding backends and fixing several tokenizer edgecases that caused invalid token sequences during constrained matching. This PR implements a new decoder backend interface, adds two concrete backends (CFG-based and Regex-based), hooks them into the OpenAI-compatibility layer and the streaming path, and includes exhaustive unit/integration tests that reproduce previously flaky cases. Key behavioral goals: (1) ensure constraints are applied deterministically across streaming boundaries, (2) avoid incorrect tokenization mismatches for multi-byte/unicode grapheme splits, and (3) provide a clear fallback strategy for unsupported constraint patterns. High level changes: implement Backend interface in serving/runtime/decoding/backend.go; add regex and cfg backends at serving/runtime/decoding/backends/{regex,cfg}_backend.go; add cross-language unit tests in redwood-openai-compat/tests/structured_constraints_test.py and redwood-sdk-python/tests/test_structured_output_constraints.py; patch tokenizer normalizer to preserve sentinel tokens and avoid merging with adjacent punctuation in tokenization (tokenizer/normalizer/edgecases.go); expose constrained-decoder configuration to API surface via redwood-openai-compat/compat_layer.go and added deprecation-safe flags to maintain backwards compatibility. Migration notes: new backend is opt-in via config constrained_decoder.type = "regex"|"cfg" and constrained_decoder.streaming_mode = "strict"|"lenient". For customers using the older inlined constraint matcher, we keep the old code path behind a feature flag for one release. Tests: unit tests cover CFG -> streaming chunk boundaries, regex lookahead across tokens, and tokenizer cases for emojis, zero-width joiners, and legacy byte-bom. Integration tests run against the OpenAI-compat test harness and a small end-to-end canary in perf-canary that validates throughput impact. CI: initial run hit a flaky tokenization test; fixed by normalizer tweak and added a deterministic random seed to the tokenizer fuzz harness. Backwards compatibility: no breaking API changes; configuration is additive. See release notes below.

release_notes: Add opt-in constrained-decoder backends (regex, CFG) for structured outputs. Fix tokenizer edgecases for unicode graphemes, zero-width joiners, and sentinel token preservation. Backward-compatible; opt-in via 'constrained_decoder.type' config. Added tests and perf canary to track overhead.
notes_for_release_manager: No API break. Recommend communicating opt-in config in this release post and running perf-canary for at least 24 hours in stage clusters before enabling by default. If customers rely on legacy behavior, keep legacy_constrained_matcher feature flag enabled for one release cycle.
